missing.text: SEEN LIGHTS? CALL THE NIGHT LINE. 1420 AM, MIDNIGHT TO FOUR. Typed, copied, and copied again.
Oil cans in rows, a calendar still on April, the register. Behind the counter a man in a pressed shirt turns a page. He has not looked at the clock once.
Two pumps on a concrete island. The counters stand at zero.
A payphone on a post, a phone book on a chain with half its pages gone.
NICKLAUS, 46, WINS MASTERS. Under the fold, smaller: County to grade the old Roswell road this summer.
One row of pins runs out east along the old road. The other runs west, off the highway, into country with nothing drawn on it.
COUNTY SHERIFF, SUBSTATION. A light under the door, and a radio turned low.
The hood is still warm. Pins in a cigar box on the dash.
The one machine turns, stops, turns. There is no basket on the bench and no one waiting.
A box office with its blind down, and a card: CLOSED.
CLOSED. THANK YOU CALICHE. FOR 31 YEARS. A letter has fallen out of the last line.
His chair pushed back. The phone's line light still blinking.
The foil has been crumpled by hand. There is a price sticker on the alien too.
